claim: geNomad classified 89-100% of natural phage sequences as viral (mean score >0.96) but only 1.9-11% of the same sequences scrambled
quote: geNomad reliably classified 89 to 100% of

claim: 19-33% of Evo 1 generations and 34-38% of Evo 2 generations were classified as viral, so Evo 2 had the stronger zero-shot baseline
quote: 19 to 33% and 34 to 38% of Evo 1 and Evo 2 generations, respectively, were classified as viral (Evo 1 mean score > 0.80, Evo 2 mean score > 0.87) depending on the prompt

claim: Generated sequences were distinct from anything in the nucleotide BLAST database yet kept high predicted coding density and phage-like features
quote: Querying generated sequences against the nucleotide BLAST database (43) revealed that generated sequences are distinct from those in nature (Fig. 1, E and F), yet they retained a high predicted coding density and genetic features reminiscent of natural phage genomes

claim: Predicted coding densities of generated sequences were reminiscent of but higher than natural sequences, and unlike scrambled natural sequences
quote: Predicted coding densities of generated sequences are reminiscent of but higher than natural sequences and unlike scrambled natural sequences.

claim: ESMFold confidence for proteins from generated sequences matched natural proteins and exceeded proteins from scrambled natural sequences
quote: predicted protein structures from generated sequences have mean predicted local distance difference test (pLDDT) scores similar to natural proteins, higher than predicted proteins from scrambled natural sequences

claim: Generated proteins showed generally low sequence identity to OpenGenome and PHROGs proteins while keeping a realistic distribution of gene annotations
quote: generally showed low sequence identity with a realistic distribution of gene annotations

claim: The design template was PhiX174, a lytic Microviridae phage with a ~5.4 kb genome, 11 genes, at least seven regulatory elements and two recognition sequences
quote: a lytic Microviridae phage with a ∼5.4–kilobase (kb) genome containing 11 genes, at least seven regulatory elements, and two recognition sequences

claim: PhiX174 and the nonpathogenic E. coli C host were chosen as a tractable and safe model; PhiX174 was the first complete DNA genome sequenced and synthesized
quote: its relatively small genomic length and rich history of experimental work (38) also make it a tractable and safe model for establishing whole-­genome design

claim: Evo 1 7B 131K and Evo 2 7B 8K were fine-tuned on about 15,000 Microviridae sequences
quote: we fine-­tuned Evo 1 7B 131K and Evo 2 7B 8K on a dataset of ∼15,000 Microviridae sequences

claim: Microviridae training genomes began with highly diverse start sequences, but all PhiX174-like genomes shared the same consensus start nucleotides
quote: Whereas the genomic start sequences of all Microviridae sequences in the training data were highly diverse, all the ΦX174-­like genomes started with the same consensus nucleotides

claim: The fine-tuned models recalled PhiX174 from a consensus-sequence prompt while the base models failed at every prompt length
quote: By contrast, the base models failed to recall ΦX174 across all tested lengths of the consensus sequence prompt.

claim: Constraints were organized into three tiers - sequence quality, tropism specificity and evolutionary diversity - with length held to 4-6 kb and GC content to 30-65%
quote: We organized these constraints into three tiers: sequence quality, tropism specificity, and evolutionary diversity.

claim: None of six widely used gene annotation tools could annotate all 11 PhiX174 genes, reflecting the difficulty of overlapping ORFs
quote: we found that none of six broadly used gene annotation tools were able to annotate all 11 genes on the wild-­type ΦX174 sequence

claim: A bespoke CDS prediction method annotated every PhiX174 gene except gene A*, which was only partially predicted
quote: that was able to fully annotate all genes in ΦX174, with the exception of gene A*, which was partially predicted

claim: The tropism constraint required generated genomes to encode spike proteins of moderate sequence identity, because host range is largely set by spike binding to host receptors
quote: Because host range is largely determined by the ability of viral spike proteins to bind host cell receptors (47, 49), we applied a tropism constraint requiring that generated genomes encode spike proteins with moderate sequence identity

claim: Diversification preferred genomes at or below 95% average amino acid identity to natural proteins, and a genetic architecture score removed genomes matching PhiX174's exact coding positions
quote: We preferred genomes with ≤95% average amino acid identity (AAI) to natural proteins, directly promoting diverged proteome sequences.

claim: After tropism filtering up to 100% of Evo 1 SFT generations and 53.8% of Evo 2 SFT generations were retained; after diversification filtering, 10.4% and 17.2%
quote: After tropism filtering, we retained as much as 100% of the Evo 1 SFT generations and 53.8% of the Evo 2 SFT generations. After diversification-­based filtering, we retained as much as 10.4% of Evo 1 generations and 17.2% of

claim: Prompts of nine or more consensus nucleotides produced memorized PhiX174 recall at low temperature, while one or two nucleotides gave too little conditioning
quote: We found that prompting with the first nine or more nucleotides from the ΦX174 consensus sequence (Fig. 2D) led to simple, memorized recall of ΦX174 with minimal diversity at low sampling temperatures

claim: Steering toward diverse PhiX174-like sequences needed a prompt of about four to nine nucleotides and a sampling temperature of 0.7 to 0.9
quote: steering toward diverse, ΦX174-­like sequences required carefully tuning the length of the consensus-­sequence prompt to be around four to nine nucleotides and the sampling temperature to be in the 0.7 to 0.9 range

claim: Shannon diversity rose with both temperature and prompt length without costing retention through the diversification filters
quote: with Shannon diversity, a measure of biodiversity (50), increasing alongside temperature and prompt length (Fig. 2J). This diversity did not come at the cost of design quality, with a high percentage of sequences being retained after applying our diversification filters

claim: 302 candidate genomes were curated, spanning 4-6 kb, with amino acid identities to natural proteins as low as 63% and spike identities largely above 85%
quote: we curated a set of 302 diverse generated phage genome candidates (figs. S7 and S8). We designated these phages “Evo-­Φ” followed by a numeric sequence identifier. These genomes spanned 4 to 6 kb in length, had AAIs to natural proteins as low as 63%, and retained spike protein sequence identities largely above 85%

claim: CheckV classified more than 87% of the generated sequences as High Quality or Complete, and most candidates shared over 40% nucleotide identity with PhiX174
quote: CheckV, a tool for assessing the quality of viral sequences, classified >87% of the generated sequences as High Quality or Complete

claim: Most generated genomes encoded 11 genes in total, with 10 preserving synteny with PhiX174
quote: Most genomes encoded 11 genes in total, with 10 genes preserving synteny with ΦX174

claim: 285 of the 302 generated genomes were successfully synthesized and assembled; the 17 failures were due to high-complexity DNA synthesis
quote: we successfully synthesized and assembled 285 out of 302 generated genomes; the remaining failed because of high-­complexity DNA synthesis

claim: 16 of the generated genomes inhibited growth of E. coli C, the viability readout
quote: we observed 16 generated phage transformations that inhibited growth of E. coli C

claim: None of the 285 assemblies inhibited growth in E. coli K-12, supporting the robustness of the tropism constraint filter
quote: When transformed in E. coli K-­12, none of the 285 assemblies resulted in growth inhibition, supporting the robustness of the tropism constraint filter

claim: Of the 16 viable candidates, nine carried no acquired mutations and seven picked up SNVs or deletions during synthesis or rebooting
quote: Sequence-­verification of the 16 candidates revealed nine genomes with no acquired mutations, whereas the other seven acquired some single-­nucleotide variants (SNVs) or deletions during synthesis or rebooting

claim: Four of the seven acquired mutation sets moved the phage closer to its nearest natural genome and some were essential for viability
quote: Four out of the seven sets of acquired mutations made the phages more similar to their nearest natural genome, and some were essential for viability, suggesting selective pressure for some sequences observed in nature

claim: Viability rates were 12 of 227 (5.3%) for Evo 1 sequences and 4 of 58 (6.9%) for Evo 2 sequences
quote: 12 out of 227 (5.3%) tested sequences generated by Evo 1 and 4 out of 58 (6.9%) generated by Evo 2 were viable

claim: Viability rose with similarity to natural genomes, reaching 46.2% in the 98-100% similarity band
quote: Viability tended to increase with sequence similarity to natural genomes, with as high as 46.2% of generated phages viable in the 98 to 100% sequence similarity range

claim: Across eight E. coli strains, PhiX174 and 15 of the 16 generated phages also inhibited E. coli W, a host not previously associated with PhiX174, with no inhibition in the other six strains
quote: ΦX174 and 15 out of 16 of the generated phages could also inhibit growth in E. coli W, a host not previously associated with ΦX174 (47, 56), although they did so with much more variation in growth kinetics

claim: Against nearest natural genomes the generated phages carried 49-143 synonymous, 14-51 nonsynonymous, 0-3 indel and 0-12 intergenic substitutions, at 93.2-98.8% similarity
quote: generated phages contained between 49 and 143 synonymous substitutions, 14 and 51 nonsynonymous substitutions, 0 and 3 indels, and 0 and 12 intergenic substitutions, with overall sequence similarities between 93.2 and 98.8%

claim: Generated phages showed the most within-group diversity of any dataset compared and the broadest genome length range, 99-105% of PhiX174's length
quote: group compared with the natural phage datasets as well as the broadest distribution of genome lengths, between 99 and 105% of the lengths of their nearest natural genomes

claim: Generated phage likelihoods under an MSA of PhiX174-like phages were far lower than site-independently sampled phages from the same MSA, so the models go beyond simple sequence statistics
quote: The likelihoods of generated phages under a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of ΦX174-­like phages were far lower than those of site-­independently

claim: A null model from PhiX174's ~20% nonsynonymous lethality predicted only 2.3% survival for genomes with under 25 nonsynonymous mutations and near zero above that
quote: allowed us to estimate that the expected survival rate of mutated genomes would only be 2.3% on average for the generated genomes with <25 nonsynonymous mutations and close to 0.0% for higher mutational burdens

claim: Observed success rates were 60.0% (3/5) up to 25 nonsynonymous mutations, 26.2% (11/42) for 25-50 and 14.3% (2/14) for 50-75, far above the null
quote: The success rate of our tested genome designs was 60.0% (3/5) for genomes with up to 25 nonsynonymous mutations, 26.2% (11/42) for those with 25 to 50 non­ synonymous mutations, and 14.3% (2/14) for those with 50 to 75 nonsynonymous mutations.

claim: Mutations in nonviable genomes were enriched in genes H, A and B and depleted in gene F
quote: mutations in nonviable genomes were enriched in genes H, A, and B and depleted in gene F

claim: Mutations in 13 of the generated genomes could not be recapitulated from any known natural sequence
quote: Mutations in 13 of the generated genomes could not be recapitulated from any known natural sequences

claim: Deleting the novel noncoding region was lethal in Evo-Phi2483 but tolerated in Evo-Phi2147 and Evo-Phi2498, and deleting the downstream gene J in Evo-Phi63 was lethal
quote: Removal of the noncoding region in Evo-­Φ2483 was lethal, whereas analogous deletions in Evo-­Φ2147 and Evo-­Φ2498 remained viable (fig. S18). We also found that deletion of the downstream gene J in Evo-­Φ63 was lethal.

claim: The most mutated elements across the 16 genomes were promoter A, gene J and terminator J, at mean rates of 0.054, 0.052 and 0.043
quote: The most mutated elements amongst the 16 genomes were promoter A, gene J, and terminator J, with average mutation rates of 0.054, 0.052, and 0.043, respectively

claim: In Evo-Phi36 gene J, a genome-packaging protein that also supports the capsid, was replaced by a shorter homolog from the distant phage G4
quote: We observed that in Evo-­Φ36, gene J, a genome-­packaging protein that also supports the capsid (63), was replaced with a shorter homologous protein found in phage G4, differing by four synonymous SNVs.

claim: G4 is only 63.0% similar to PhiX174 while Evo-Phi36 is 97.1% similar; the G4 J protein is 25 amino acids against PhiX174's 38
quote: G4 is a distantly related Microvirus with only 63.0% sequence similarity to ΦX174 (fig. S20A) (64), whereas Evo-­Φ36 shares 97.1% similarity with ΦX174. The G4 J protein is 25 amino acids long compared with the ΦX174 J protein, which is 38 amino acids long

claim: Swapping G4's J into PhiX174 is known to be nonviable, yet Evo-Phi36 is viable; its J worked in the nearest natural genome NC51 but stayed lethal in PhiX174, implicating up to 58 enabling mutations
quote: Evo-­Φ36 J was viable in NC51, whereas it remained lethal in ΦX174 (fig. S20, C to E), indicating up to 58 possible mutations across Evo-­Φ36’s genome that enabled its functionality

claim: Cryo-EM resolved PhiX174 to 2.8 A and Evo-Phi36 to 2.9 A
quote: we solved the structure of ΦX174 to a resolution of 2.8 Å and that of Evo-­Φ36 to a resolution of 2.9 Å by cryo–electron microscopy

claim: Evo-Phi36's J kept a similar C-terminal capsid binding mode despite a phenylalanine-to-tyrosine substitution, but 14 N-terminal residues could not be resolved
quote: Despite introducing more polarity at the capsid-­J interface by substitution of the C-­terminal phenylalanine (F) with a tyrosine (Y), Evo-­Φ36 J maintains a similar overall binding mode at its C terminus

claim: Evo-Phi2483, Evo-Phi69, Evo-Phi108 and Evo-Phi111 showed strong lytic phenotypes comparable to natural phages, while Evo-Phi63 lysed most slowly and shallowly
quote: Evo-­Φ63 generally exhibited the slowest and most shallow lysis compared with that of all other phages.

claim: Generated phages spanned a broader range of lysis kinetics than the natural phages measured alongside them
quote: Generated phages also showed a broader range of phenotypes across the measured lysis kinetics relative to that of natural phages

claim: In equal-MOI coinfection, Evo-Phi69, Evo-Phi100 and Evo-Phi111 outcompeted the rest; Evo-Phi69 reached cumulative fold changes of ~10X to 41X at 6 hours, while Evo-Phi36 and Evo-Phi108 fell most
quote: Evo-­Φ69 specifically had the highest FC in the mixed population compared with that of nearly all other generated phages and ΦX174, with cumulative FCs between ∼10X and 41X after 6 hours of infection, whereas Evo-­Φ36 and Evo-­Φ108 had the largest decreases in FC over time.

claim: No correlation was found between a phage's naturalness and its competitiveness, so naturalness is not a reliable fitness predictor
quote: We found no correlation between the naturalness of each phage and their relative competitiveness (fig. S29), suggesting that naturalness is not a reliable predictor of fitness for generated phages.

claim: Two independently evolved resistant E. coli C strains both carried waa operon mutations affecting LPS synthesis: CR1 a waaT L259W missense, CR2 a single-base deletion at nucleotide 485 giving a premature stop
quote: CR1 contained a missense mutation, L259W (Leu259 → Trp), in the waaT gene and strain CR2 contained a single base deletion at nucleotide position 485 of waaT, resulting in a premature stop codon followed

claim: The generated cocktail inhibited CR1 after one passage and CR2 after two and held for at least five passages, while PhiX174 alone and the 16-phage natural cocktail failed on both even after five passages
quote: The generated phage cocktail was able to successfully inhibit growth of strain CR1 after a single passage and CR2 after two passages and sustain growth inhibition for at least five passages. By contrast, ΦX174 alone and the natural phage cocktail both could not inhibit growth of any resistant strains even after five passages

claim: Evo-PhiR1's genome was composable from five segments of Evo-Phi111 and Evo-Phi114 bar two capsid SNVs; Evo-PhiR2's from four segments of Evo-Phi111, Evo-Phi114 and Evo-Phi2147 bar one
quote: Sequence alignment revealed that all of Evo-­ΦR1’s genome could be collectively composed from five segments of Evo-­Φ111 and Evo-­Φ114 except for two SNVs in the major capsid protein

claim: Both resistance-breaking phages carried 15 nonsynonymous capsid and spike mutations absent from PhiX174, 14 of them Evo-generated, mostly on the virion's outer surface
quote: we observed 15 nonsynonymous mutations across the capsid and spike proteins that were not present in ΦX174, 14 of which were generated by Evo

claim: Evo-Phi63's genome is 5% (268 nucleotides) longer than PhiX174, a property previous systematic efforts had struggled to increase
quote: the genome of Evo-­Φ63, that is 5% (268 nucleotides) longer than ΦX174

claim: Evo-Phi2147 is only ~93% similar to known natural genomes, below the <95% threshold some taxonomic guidelines use to delineate a new phage species
quote: the genome of Evo-­Φ2147 has ∼93% sequence similarity to known natural genomes. Some sequence-­based taxonomic guidelines use <95% sequence similarity as one threshold to delineate new bacteriophage species

claim: The authors state that generating phage genomes raises biosafety, biocontainment and biosecurity considerations and that future whole-genome design work should consult safety and security professionals throughout the project lifecycle
quote: Groups conducting future whole-­genome design work should consult both safety and security professionals throughout the project lifecycle.
